subject: Capacity hedging options and fast-fallback plan for Atlas Labs deal
messages:
From: Maya Chen <procurement@atlaslabs.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-06T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated pool sizing & target launch window (Q3)

Karthik —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We are moving this through procurement and need to lock on two things to get an LOI across the finish line: (1) recommended dedicated pool sizing for our 100k MAU prediction (chat + embeddings workloads) and (2) realistic procurement timings for any hardware commitments / OEM quotes you require to guarantee a Q3 launch.

High-level constraints: we will need a mixture of reserved capacity and cloud backstop for the first 90 days; security team will only accept a private/dedicated pool for PII-sensitive routes. Procurement timeline is tight — we need an actionable path by April 15.

Attached is a short RFP and peak traffic profile. Please share an options table (best/likely/worst), lead-times for OEM orders, and any recommended cloud fallback partners you can put on a provisional hold.

Thanks,
Maya Chen
Procurement Manager, Atlas Labs
[Attachment: Atlas_RFP_Q2-2027.pdf (application/pdf)]

From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Maya Chen <procurement@atlaslabs.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-07T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated pool sizing & target launch window (Q3)

Maya —

Appreciate the RFP and timeline. Quick read and initial asks from our side so we can give a crisp options table by EOD Apr 12: 

1) Can you confirm the 99th percentile concurrency estimate in the RFP (you list 45 concurrent chats/min at peak) — that drives KV cache sizing.
2) Do you expect long context sessions (>8k tokens) for the PII routes? That affects GPU SKU choice.
3) Any inbound traffic region constraints (we assume US-only for now).

High-level from us now: we can propose three delivery lanes — (A) Reserved Dedicated Pool (preferred by security), (B) Hybrid: smaller dedicated pool + cloud quota as backstop, (C) Cloud-first with on-demand migration to Dedicated in month 2. Each lane has different lead-times and risk.

OEM lead-time reality: for full-slate procurement (new racks / specific SKU orders) expect 16–24 weeks from PO to in-rack availability today. We can accelerate partial shipments if the OEM has available sub-lots (see OmenTech note we requested) but that typically adds ~10–20% premium.

Cloud backstop: Ben has a tentative hold with BigCloud (cloudsales@bigcloud.example.com) for ephemeral capacity. We can hold a provisional quota for 60 days if procurement signs a conditional LOI.

I'm looping Neha to sketch the sizing options and Ben to confirm the cloud hold. We'll return an options matrix and recommended canary plan (30d smoke + burst window) by Apr 12.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

On Tue, Apr 6, 2027 at 09:12 AM Maya Chen <procurement@atlaslabs.com> wrote:
> Karthik —
> 
> Thanks again for the demo last week...

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-08T08:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated pool sizing & target launch window (Q3)

Adding color from capacity ops: 

- Cloud backstop: I spoke with BigCloud; they can provision a soft-hold for a 60-day window but need a not-to-exceed commit and a contact PO. They can do ephemeral instances in the same region as Atlas with ~48–72 hour lead on spin-up.

- OEM quote: OmenTech (Rajiv Patel) promised a preliminary 50-unit quote for our standard 80GB TCU in ~48 hours. If Atlas requires a dedicated cage (on-prem style install with networking/colocation), add 4–6 weeks for rack integration.

Proposal: deliver a three-row options table to Atlas: 
  1) Fast-path Hybrid — 8-node dedicated pool (canary) + cloud backstop for peak (2–4 weeks to run canary using cloud; 6–8 weeks for first OEM tranche)
  2) Staged Dedicated — 24-node dedicated pool staggered over 3 shipments (6–12 weeks between tranches)
  3) Full Reserve — 48-node commitment (16–24 weeks OEM lead)

I'll push the BigCloud contact to put the hold under my rep name and share contact info if they want to move. Also attaching the preliminary OEM stub they sent.

Ben Carter
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: OmenTech_prelim_quote_TCUs_20270410.pdf (application/pdf)]

From: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-09T11:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Capacity hedging options and fast-fallback plan for Atlas Labs deal

Team —

Good summary. Two tactical asks from me before we send the options table to Atlas: 

1) Get two OEM quotes with explicit staggered-delivery pricing (one from OmenTech, one alternative). We need line-item lead times per tranche, premium for expedited partial shipments, and warranty/return terms.

2) Draft an ops runbook for the canary: security sign-off checklist, roll-forward/rollback metrics, and a pre-authorized cloud backfill trigger (who calls it and what SLA triggers). Keep that runbook one page.

Deliverables & owners: 
- OEM quote chase: Ben (primary) / Karthik (escalation) — target Apr 11 COB.
- Canary runbook + sizing assumptions: Neha — target Apr 11 COB.
- Options matrix + recommended sign: Karthik — target Apr 12 morning.

If we can get the two OEM quotes by Apr 11 we'll include real lead-times and a recommended tranche cadence. If not, be explicit about assumptions.

Lauren Bishop
VP, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Rajiv Patel <rajiv.patel@omentech.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@atlaslabs.com
Date: 2027-04-11T16:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: OEM quote / partial shipment feasibility

Ben/Karthik —

Thanks for the heads-up. Quick update from OmenTech supply desk: current lead-time for new 80GB TCU orders is 18 weeks for full production runs. We can do an expedited partial tranche (10 units) in ~7–9 weeks if Atlas can accept a mixed SKU arrival (some 80GB TCUs + interim 48GB units) — mixed-SKU integration is supported but will require our cross-compatibility kit and a short validation window (~72 hours per tranche). Expedited partials incur a 12% premium on unit price and an additional freight expedite fee.

I'll upload the formal preliminary quote to your drive (link below) and can follow up with full T&Cs once we confirm estimated PO sizes.

Regards,
Rajiv Patel
Director, Strategic Accounts — OmenTech
[Attachment: OmenTech_prelim_quote_TCUs_20270411.pdf (application/pdf)]
